addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.
- aws-billing-and-cost-management: Analyze AWS costs, find savings, manage budgets, evaluate Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, right-size EC2/Lambda/RDS/EBS with Compute Optimizer, look up service pricing, query CUR with Athena, detect cost anomalies, scope costs to billing views, and monitor Free Tier usage. Triggers on: AWS bill, cost analysis, reduce spend, savings plan, reserved instance, right-size, budget alert, cost optimization, pricing, free tier, cost anomaly, CUR, cost audit, billing view, billing view ARN.

Applies when creating APIs, selecting Building Blocks (KVStore, DistributedTable, Database, AuthBasic, AuthCognito, Realtime, AsyncJob, FileBucket, etc.), running local development, or deploying AWS Blocks applications. Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.
- aws-cdk: Authors, deploys, and troubleshoots AWS infrastructure using CDK with TypeScript or Python. Covers best practices, stack architecture, and construct patterns. Always use when writing CDK constructs, bootstrapping environments, running cdk deploy/synth/diff, fixing CDK or CloudFormation errors, planning stack structure, importing existing resources, resolving drift, or refactoring stacks without resource replacement.
- aws-cloudformation: Author, validate, and troubleshoot AWS CloudFormation templates. Covers template authoring with secure defaults, pre-deployment validation (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, change sets), and root-cause diagnosis of failed stacks using CloudFormation events and CloudTrail correlation.
- aws-containers: Deploys and operates containerized workloads on ECS, Fargate, and ECR. Covers task definitions, Fargate services, ECR repository setup and lifecycle policies, ECS Exec debugging, service scaling, deployment strategies, load balancer integration, and logging configuration. Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.
- aws-messaging-and-streaming: Guides use of AWS messaging and streaming services. Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.
- aws-observability: Builds, configures, debugs, and optimizes AWS observability with CloudWatch (Log Insights, Metrics, Alarms, Dashboards, EMF), X-Ray, CloudTrail, and ADOT (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry), AND enables/onboards services to Application Signals using ADOT auto-instrumentation SDKs. Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. 1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/C4illin/ConvertX
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0
7	  port: 3000
8	  vm: m1.medium
9	  flavor_id: "3"
10	  database: none (the app is SQLite-only; the volume IS the database)
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: convertx
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST PERSON TO POST /register OWNS THE INSTANCE, AND ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false DOES NOT STOP THEM. This is the quirk that would break the deploy, and it is by design rather than a bug. src/pages/user.tsx:16 reads FIRST_RUN once at module load (true when the users table is empty), and :186 gates registration on `if (!ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION && !FIRST_RUN)`, so while FIRST_RUN holds the flag is bypassed and the account is created anyway. There is also no admin ROLE to grant: src/db/db.ts:9-13 shows the users table is (id, email, password) and nothing else, so the first account is simply the only account, and it is the administrator by virtue of being the one that exists. The window opens the moment redu's hostname resolves and NO SETTING CLOSES IT. The only thing that closes it is claiming the account. Do that as part of the deploy, before you hand over the URL, then run the check script in the body of this file to prove it took."
18	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH BEFORE THE ACCOUNT IS CLAIMED: GET / returns 302 to /setup (src/pages/root.tsx:23-25) and /setup serves a Create your account form to anyone (user.tsx:68-128). GET /healthcheck is deliberately unauthenticated and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"} on any instance. Everything else, upload, convert, download, history and account, requires a valid auth cookie. AFTER the account is claimed, GET / and GET /register both 302 to /login and the setup page is unreachable. Note public/robots.txt ships Disallow: / for the whole app, which discourages crawlers and protects nothing: assume the URL is discoverable the moment it exists."
19	  - "⛔ NEVER SET ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME. Upstream's own comment on it says `only set this to true locally`, and the reason is worth spelling out. src/pages/root.tsx:33-57 hands every anonymous visitor a freshly signed 24-hour cookie and full use of the service, and src/index.tsx:30 sets maxRequestBodySize to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so there is no upload size limit of any kind. On a public URL that combination is an open disk-fill and CPU-burn primitive against the user's own VM, running ffmpeg, LibreOffice and ImageMagick on files a stranger chose. It defaults to false (src/helpers/env.ts:6-7); leave it there. UNAUTHENTICATED_USER_SHARING only matters when it is on, and would additionally pool every anonymous visitor's conversion history into one shared account."
20	  - "⛔ GENERATE YOUR OWN JWT_SECRET AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. THIS IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. Two ways to get it wrong and they fail differently. Leave it UNSET and src/pages/user.tsx:25 falls back to randomUUID() at every boot, so every session is invalidated on every container restart and the symptom reads as a broken login rather than a missing variable. COPY THE ONE IN THE README, or the one in upstream's compose.yaml, and you have shipped a signing key that is published in a repo with 18.5k stars: anyone who has read the README can mint a valid auth cookie for user id 1 and walk in. Generate one long random value of your own, pass it, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy."
21	  - "⛔ LEAVE HTTP_ALLOWED=false. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and the public URL is https, so the Secure session cookie set at user.tsx:229 and :354 (`secure: !HTTP_ALLOWED`) works correctly. The README suggests setting HTTP_ALLOWED=true as the fix for `can't login`, which is right for a plain-HTTP LAN box and wrong here: on a public internet hostname it downgrades the session cookie for no benefit. If login genuinely fails on redu, the cause is something else."
22	  - "⛔ THERE IS NO DATABASE OPTION. DO NOT PROVISION A MANAGED POSTGRES FOR THIS. src/db/db.ts:2-5 opens bun:sqlite at the hardcoded path ./data/mydb.sqlite with no env var to redirect it, and no other driver exists anywhere in the source. A managed database would bill at GBP 0.0174/hr and hold nothing. The volume IS the database, which makes the next quirk the most important one in this file after the ownership race."
23	  - "⛔ ONE VOLUME ON /app/data, AND USE A NAMED VOLUME, NOT A BIND MOUNT. Everything durable lives under it: the sqlite file (src/db/db.ts:5), every upload (./data/uploads/, src/index.tsx:22) and every converted output (./data/output/, :23). Without it a redeploy loses the accounts, the history and every file, and the instance comes back on /setup with the ownership window reopened. Prefer a named volume over upstream's `./data` bind mount for two reasons: a path inside the project directory is exactly what a source re-upload replaces, and the container runs as root (the Dockerfile has no USER directive), which is what produces the `unable to open database file` error the README tells you to fix with chown. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a negative check alone is worthless: see the docker inspect block in the body of this file, whose first command exists purely to prove the container name resolved before the second command's answer is allowed to mean anything."
24	  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT HERE, NOT RAM, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS m1.medium RATHER THAN m1.small. Docker Hub's tag API reported full_size 1,554,975,448 bytes for v0.18.0 on 2026-08-17, about 1.55 GB COMPRESSED; upstream publishes no unpacked figure and this recipe has not been run, so the on-disk size is unknown but certainly larger, because Dockerfile:45-100 installs texlive with three extra collections, LibreOffice, Calibre, Inkscape, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, Ghostscript, ffmpeg and markitdown. On top of that every conversion keeps BOTH the uploaded input and the generated output on the same disk until the cleaner runs. m1.small ships 20 GB and that is not enough headroom to be comfortable; m1.medium ships 40 GB. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy, so put this in front of the user BEFORE sizing. Record the real numbers on the first run."
25	  - "AUTO_DELETE_EVERY_N_HOURS IS THE ONLY GARBAGE COLLECTOR, AND SETTING IT TO 0 TURNS IT OFF. It defaults to 24 (src/helpers/env.ts:9-11). src/index.tsx:72-97 runs a setTimeout chain from boot that deletes every job older than N hours, together with its upload and output directories, every N hours. Set it to 0 and nothing is ever deleted and the disk grows until it is full, which on a file converter is a matter of use rather than of time. Keep it at 24 or lower, and say plainly in the handover that converted files are TEMPORARY: this is a converter, not storage."
26	  - "SET MAX_CONVERT_PROCESS TO A SMALL NUMBER. It defaults to 0, which means unlimited (src/helpers/env.ts:19-22), and 0 is not merely a permissive cap: src/converters/main.ts:142-148 returns the whole file list as ONE chunk when the size is 0, and :163 then starts every file in that chunk concurrently. A single job containing two hundred files therefore launches two hundred ffmpeg or LibreOffice processes at once, which on a 2 vCPU / 4 GB VM is an out-of-memory kill rather than a slow conversion. 2 to 4 is a sane value; it costs throughput on big batches and buys the instance staying up."
27	  - "ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION: LEAVE IT AT ITS DEFAULT OF false (src/helpers/env.ts:1-2) unless the user actually wants more accounts. With it off and one account existing, GET /register 302s to /login and POST /register 302s to /login, so nobody else can sign up. It protects the SECOND account onward and does nothing whatsoever about the first: see the ownership quirk at the top. If the user does want extra accounts, turn it on deliberately, after claiming the first one, and understand that anyone who finds the URL can then register."
28	  - "PIN THE IMAGE, AND MIND THE LEADING v IN THE TAG. Use ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 (or c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 on Docker Hub, which carries the same tags). The compose in upstream's README writes `image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx` with NO tag at all, which resolves to :latest and will silently cross a release on the next pull. On 2026-08-17 Docker Hub reported identical full_size and last_updated for v0.18.0 and latest, so they are the same build today and will not be after the next release. Note the tags are v0.18.0 and v0.17.0 with the v, unlike several other entries in this library. There is also a :main tag built from every push to the main branch; it is not a release and does not belong in a recipe."
29	  - "PORT 3000, AND THE HEALTH PROBE IS /healthcheck. Dockerfile:109 exposes 3000 and src/index.tsx:68 listens on process.env.PORT || 3000. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. src/pages/healthcheck.tsx is explicitly `auth: false` and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"}, which makes it the right thing to gate every verification on: it proves you reached ConvertX rather than redu's proxy, which answers 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts."
30	  - "LEAVE WEBROOT EMPTY. src/index.tsx:32 passes it as the Elysia prefix, so it moves every route and every generated link under that path. It exists for people mounting ConvertX at example.com/convert on a shared hostname. On a dedicated redu hostname there is nothing to prefix and a stray value gives 404s everywhere, including on /healthcheck, which then makes a healthy instance look dead."
31	  - "ALSO WORTH SETTING, NONE OF THEM LOAD-BEARING: TZ, which only formats dates in the UI, and LANGUAGE as a BCP 47 tag for the same reason. FFMPEG_ARGS and FFMPEG_OUTPUT_ARGS pass raw arguments to ffmpeg; hardware acceleration flags are pointless on a redu VM, which has no GPU passthrough, so leave them unset. HIDE_HISTORY hides the history page and does not restrict anything."
32	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. src/db/db.ts:7-31 creates the three tables on first import if sqlite_master is empty, then applies a PRAGMA user_version migration, then sets WAL mode. First boot is otherwise just the image pull, which is the slow part."
33	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.028/hr, roughly GBP 20 a month, and it fits inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), NO database, port 3000, and a named volume on /app/data. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared: pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.medium, and if you do accept a larger flavor, accept it for the DISK rather than because the planner suggested it."
34	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and you very much do not want to: building this image installs texlive, LibreOffice and Calibre on the VM. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally against the pinned image, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
35	  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, verified from the LICENSE file, which is the full GNU Affero General Public License version 3. Self-hosting an unmodified published image for your own use is exactly what it is for. The one clause worth a sentence is section 13: if you MODIFY ConvertX and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Deploying the official image unmodified leaves that satisfied by upstream's own repository. redu is not the operator here; the user runs their own instance in their own account."
36	  - "DELETING IT TAKES EVERYTHING WITH IT, WHICH IS DIFFERENT FROM MOST ENTRIES IN THIS LIBRARY. There is no managed database left behind and nothing left billing, because there never was one. delete_deployment removes the app VM and with it the volume holding the sqlite file, the account, the history and every converted file. Say that plainly before deleting; there is no second copy anywhere."
37	---
38	
39	# Self-host ConvertX on redu
40	
41	A file converter you own: over a thousand format pairs, one container, a public HTTPS URL, and no
42	files leaving your own VM. About GBP 20 a month.
43	
44	## What this deploys
45	
46	- **ConvertX** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
47	- **One volume on `/app/data`**, which holds the SQLite database, every upload and every
48	  converted file. This app has no database server; the volume is the whole of its storage.
49	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
50	
51	About GBP 0.028/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
52	
53	## Deploy
54	
55	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
56	directory containing this file:
57	
58	    Read redu.md and deploy ConvertX on redu.
59	
60	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
61	
62	## The three that actually break it
63	
64	**Nobody owns it until you do.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the account,
65	and `ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false` does not stop them: the source bypasses that flag while the
66	users table is empty. There is no admin role to grant and no setting that closes the window. The
67	only thing that closes it is claiming the account, which the recipe does before handing over the
68	URL. The script below proves it took.
69

87	# Usage:  HOST=convertx-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud bash check-claimed.sh

90	B=$(mktemp)

94	code=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthcheck")

96	  502) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly."; exit 2 ;;
97	  200) : ;;
98	  *)   echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck answered $code, not 200."; exit 2 ;;
99	esac
100	grep -q '"status":"ok"' "$B" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck body is not ConvertX's."; exit 2; }
101	
102	# (2) Positive control for step 3. A claimed instance renders a login page that names itself.
103	#     If this fails, the redirect check below cannot be read as a pass.
104	lcode=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
105	grep -q 'ConvertX | Login' "$B" ||
106	  { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login answered $lcode and did not render ConvertX's login page."; exit 2; }
107	echo "OK: ConvertX is up and its login page renders."
108	
109	# (3) The assertion. Anonymous GET / must land on /login. /setup is the UNCLAIMED state:
110	#     it serves a create-your-account form to whoever asks.
111	loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/")

113	  */setup) echo "FAIL: / redirects to /setup. THIS INSTANCE IS UNCLAIMED. Claim it now."; rm -f "$B"; exit 1 ;;
114	  */login) echo "PASS: / redirects to /login, so an account exists and the window is shut." ;;

116	esac

120	if [ "$rcode" = "302" ]; then
121	  echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] /register redirects, so ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION is off."
122	else
123	  echo "WARN: GET /register answered $rcode, so registration is OPEN to anyone. Intended?"

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/C4illin/ConvertX
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: none (the app is SQLite-only; the volume IS the database)
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: convertx
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST PERSON TO POST /register OWNS THE INSTANCE, AND ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false DOES NOT STOP THEM. This is the quirk that would break the deploy, and it is by design rather than a bug. src/pages/user.tsx:16 reads FIRST_RUN once at module load (true when the users table is empty), and :186 gates registration on `if (!ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION && !FIRST_RUN)`, so while FIRST_RUN holds the flag is bypassed and the account is created anyway. There is also no admin ROLE to grant: src/db/db.ts:9-13 shows the users table is (id, email, password) and nothing else, so the first account is simply the only account, and it is the administrator by virtue of being the one that exists. The window opens the moment redu's hostname resolves and NO SETTING CLOSES IT. The only thing that closes it is claiming the account. Do that as part of the deploy, before you hand over the URL, then run the check script in the body of this file to prove it took."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH BEFORE THE ACCOUNT IS CLAIMED: GET / returns 302 to /setup (src/pages/root.tsx:23-25) and /setup serves a Create your account form to anyone (user.tsx:68-128). GET /healthcheck is deliberately unauthenticated and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"} on any instance. Everything else, upload, convert, download, history and account, requires a valid auth cookie. AFTER the account is claimed, GET / and GET /register both 302 to /login and the setup page is unreachable. Note public/robots.txt ships Disallow: / for the whole app, which discourages crawlers and protects nothing: assume the URL is discoverable the moment it exists."
  - "⛔ NEVER SET ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME. Upstream's own comment on it says `only set this to true locally`, and the reason is worth spelling out. src/pages/root.tsx:33-57 hands every anonymous visitor a freshly signed 24-hour cookie and full use of the service, and src/index.tsx:30 sets maxRequestBodySize to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so there is no upload size limit of any kind. On a public URL that combination is an open disk-fill and CPU-burn primitive against the user's own VM, running ffmpeg, LibreOffice and ImageMagick on files a stranger chose. It defaults to false (src/helpers/env.ts:6-7); leave it there. UNAUTHENTICATED_USER_SHARING only matters when it is on, and would additionally pool every anonymous visitor's conversion history into one shared account."
  - "⛔ GENERATE YOUR OWN JWT_SECRET AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. THIS IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. Two ways to get it wrong and they fail differently. Leave it UNSET and src/pages/user.tsx:25 falls back to randomUUID() at every boot, so every session is invalidated on every container restart and the symptom reads as a broken login rather than a missing variable. COPY THE ONE IN THE README, or the one in upstream's compose.yaml, and you have shipped a signing key that is published in a repo with 18.5k stars: anyone who has read the README can mint a valid auth cookie for user id 1 and walk in. Generate one long random value of your own, pass it, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy."
  - "⛔ LEAVE HTTP_ALLOWED=false. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and the public URL is https, so the Secure session cookie set at user.tsx:229 and :354 (`secure: !HTTP_ALLOWED`) works correctly. The README suggests setting HTTP_ALLOWED=true as the fix for `can't login`, which is right for a plain-HTTP LAN box and wrong here: on a public internet hostname it downgrades the session cookie for no benefit. If login genuinely fails on redu, the cause is something else."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO DATABASE OPTION. DO NOT PROVISION A MANAGED POSTGRES FOR THIS. src/db/db.ts:2-5 opens bun:sqlite at the hardcoded path ./data/mydb.sqlite with no env var to redirect it, and no other driver exists anywhere in the source. A managed database would bill at GBP 0.0174/hr and hold nothing. The volume IS the database, which makes the next quirk the most important one in this file after the ownership race."
  - "⛔ ONE VOLUME ON /app/data, AND USE A NAMED VOLUME, NOT A BIND MOUNT. Everything durable lives under it: the sqlite file (src/db/db.ts:5), every upload (./data/uploads/, src/index.tsx:22) and every converted output (./data/output/, :23). Without it a redeploy loses the accounts, the history and every file, and the instance comes back on /setup with the ownership window reopened. Prefer a named volume over upstream's `./data` bind mount for two reasons: a path inside the project directory is exactly what a source re-upload replaces, and the container runs as root (the Dockerfile has no USER directive), which is what produces the `unable to open database file` error the README tells you to fix with chown. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a negative check alone is worthless: see the docker inspect block in the body of this file, whose first command exists purely to prove the container name resolved before the second command's answer is allowed to mean anything."
  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT HERE, NOT RAM, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS m1.medium RATHER THAN m1.small. Docker Hub's tag API reported full_size 1,554,975,448 bytes for v0.18.0 on 2026-08-17, about 1.55 GB COMPRESSED; upstream publishes no unpacked figure and this recipe has not been run, so the on-disk size is unknown but certainly larger, because Dockerfile:45-100 installs texlive with three extra collections, LibreOffice, Calibre, Inkscape, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, Ghostscript, ffmpeg and markitdown. On top of that every conversion keeps BOTH the uploaded input and the generated output on the same disk until the cleaner runs. m1.small ships 20 GB and that is not enough headroom to be comfortable; m1.medium ships 40 GB. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy, so put this in front of the user BEFORE sizing. Record the real numbers on the first run."
  - "AUTO_DELETE_EVERY_N_HOURS IS THE ONLY GARBAGE COLLECTOR, AND SETTING IT TO 0 TURNS IT OFF. It defaults to 24 (src/helpers/env.ts:9-11). src/index.tsx:72-97 runs a setTimeout chain from boot that deletes every job older than N hours, together with its upload and output directories, every N hours. Set it to 0 and nothing is ever deleted and the disk grows until it is full, which on a file converter is a matter of use rather than of time. Keep it at 24 or lower, and say plainly in the handover that converted files are TEMPORARY: this is a converter, not storage."
  - "SET MAX_CONVERT_PROCESS TO A SMALL NUMBER. It defaults to 0, which means unlimited (src/helpers/env.ts:19-22), and 0 is not merely a permissive cap: src/converters/main.ts:142-148 returns the whole file list as ONE chunk when the size is 0, and :163 then starts every file in that chunk concurrently. A single job containing two hundred files therefore launches two hundred ffmpeg or LibreOffice processes at once, which on a 2 vCPU / 4 GB VM is an out-of-memory kill rather than a slow conversion. 2 to 4 is a sane value; it costs throughput on big batches and buys the instance staying up."
  - "ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION: LEAVE IT AT ITS DEFAULT OF false (src/helpers/env.ts:1-2) unless the user actually wants more accounts. With it off and one account existing, GET /register 302s to /login and POST /register 302s to /login, so nobody else can sign up. It protects the SECOND account onward and does nothing whatsoever about the first: see the ownership quirk at the top. If the user does want extra accounts, turn it on deliberately, after claiming the first one, and understand that anyone who finds the URL can then register."
  - "PIN THE IMAGE, AND MIND THE LEADING v IN THE TAG. Use ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 (or c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 on Docker Hub, which carries the same tags). The compose in upstream's README writes `image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx` with NO tag at all, which resolves to :latest and will silently cross a release on the next pull. On 2026-08-17 Docker Hub reported identical full_size and last_updated for v0.18.0 and latest, so they are the same build today and will not be after the next release. Note the tags are v0.18.0 and v0.17.0 with the v, unlike several other entries in this library. There is also a :main tag built from every push to the main branch; it is not a release and does not belong in a recipe."
  - "PORT 3000, AND THE HEALTH PROBE IS /healthcheck. Dockerfile:109 exposes 3000 and src/index.tsx:68 listens on process.env.PORT || 3000. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. src/pages/healthcheck.tsx is explicitly `auth: false` and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"}, which makes it the right thing to gate every verification on: it proves you reached ConvertX rather than redu's proxy, which answers 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts."
  - "LEAVE WEBROOT EMPTY. src/index.tsx:32 passes it as the Elysia prefix, so it moves every route and every generated link under that path. It exists for people mounting ConvertX at example.com/convert on a shared hostname. On a dedicated redu hostname there is nothing to prefix and a stray value gives 404s everywhere, including on /healthcheck, which then makes a healthy instance look dead."
  - "ALSO WORTH SETTING, NONE OF THEM LOAD-BEARING: TZ, which only formats dates in the UI, and LANGUAGE as a BCP 47 tag for the same reason. FFMPEG_ARGS and FFMPEG_OUTPUT_ARGS pass raw arguments to ffmpeg; hardware acceleration flags are pointless on a redu VM, which has no GPU passthrough, so leave them unset. HIDE_HISTORY hides the history page and does not restrict anything."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. src/db/db.ts:7-31 creates the three tables on first import if sqlite_master is empty, then applies a PRAGMA user_version migration, then sets WAL mode. First boot is otherwise just the image pull, which is the slow part."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.028/hr, roughly GBP 20 a month, and it fits inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), NO database, port 3000, and a named volume on /app/data. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared: pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.medium, and if you do accept a larger flavor, accept it for the DISK rather than because the planner suggested it."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and you very much do not want to: building this image installs texlive, LibreOffice and Calibre on the VM. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally against the pinned image, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, verified from the LICENSE file, which is the full GNU Affero General Public License version 3. Self-hosting an unmodified published image for your own use is exactly what it is for. The one clause worth a sentence is section 13: if you MODIFY ConvertX and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Deploying the official image unmodified leaves that satisfied by upstream's own repository. redu is not the operator here; the user runs their own instance in their own account."
  - "DELETING IT TAKES EVERYTHING WITH IT, WHICH IS DIFFERENT FROM MOST ENTRIES IN THIS LIBRARY. There is no managed database left behind and nothing left billing, because there never was one. delete_deployment removes the app VM and with it the volume holding the sqlite file, the account, the history and every converted file. Say that plainly before deleting; there is no second copy anywhere."

# Self-host ConvertX on redu

A file converter you own: over a thousand format pairs, one container, a public HTTPS URL, and no
files leaving your own VM. About GBP 20 a month.

## What this deploys

- **ConvertX** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **One volume on `/app/data`**, which holds the SQLite database, every upload and every
  converted file. This app has no database server; the volume is the whole of its storage.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.028/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy ConvertX on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Nobody owns it until you do.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the account,
and `ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false` does not stop them: the source bypasses that flag while the
users table is empty. There is no admin role to grant and no setting that closes the window. The
only thing that closes it is claiming the account, which the recipe does before handing over the
URL. The script below proves it took.

**Disk, not memory.** The image carries texlive, LibreOffice, Calibre, Inkscape, ImageMagick and
ffmpeg, and every conversion then keeps both the input and the output until the cleaner runs. That
is why this is an m1.medium with 40 GB rather than the cheaper 20 GB flavor. Growing it later is a
volume resize, not a redeploy.

**Everything is on the volume.** There is no managed database in this plan because ConvertX cannot
use one: it is SQLite-only, at a hardcoded path. Miss the volume and a redeploy loses the account,
the history and every file, and puts the sign-up form back on a public URL.

## Prove the instance is claimed

Run this after the deploy. It refuses to answer at all until it can show it is talking to ConvertX
rather than to redu's proxy, which returns 502 for roughly the first two and a half minutes.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a ConvertX instance is CLAIMED, i.e. that the first-account window is shut.
# Usage:  HOST=convertx-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud bash check-claimed.sh
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname, with no scheme}"
B=$(mktemp)

# (1) Gate: prove we are talking to ConvertX at all. Every assertion below is meaningless
#     against an error page, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthcheck")
case "$code" in
  502) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly."; exit 2 ;;
  200) : ;;
  *)   echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck answered $code, not 200."; exit 2 ;;
esac
grep -q '"status":"ok"' "$B" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck body is not ConvertX's."; exit 2; }

# (2) Positive control for step 3. A claimed instance renders a login page that names itself.
#     If this fails, the redirect check below cannot be read as a pass.
lcode=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
grep -q 'ConvertX | Login' "$B" ||
  { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login answered $lcode and did not render ConvertX's login page."; exit 2; }
echo "OK: ConvertX is up and its login page renders."

# (3) The assertion. Anonymous GET / must land on /login. /setup is the UNCLAIMED state:
#     it serves a create-your-account form to whoever asks.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/")
case "$loc" in
  */setup) echo "FAIL: / redirects to /setup. THIS INSTANCE IS UNCLAIMED. Claim it now."; rm -f "$B"; exit 1 ;;
  */login) echo "PASS: / redirects to /login, so an account exists and the window is shut." ;;
  *)       echo "INCONCLUSIVE: / redirected to '$loc', which is neither. Check by hand."; rm -f "$B"; exit 2 ;;
esac

# (4) And that nobody else can sign up behind you.
rcode=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/register")
if [ "$rcode" = "302" ]; then
  echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] /register redirects, so ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION is off."
else
  echo "WARN: GET /register answered $rcode, so registration is OPEN to anyone. Intended?"
fi
rm -f "$B"
```

## Prove the volume took

Both halves, on the VM. The first command exists only to prove the container name resolved: without
it, a zero from the second command could just as easily mean you typed the wrong name.

```bash
C=convertx   # or whatever the compose project named it; list with: sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'

# Positive: this must print the container's name. If it errors, STOP, everything below is void.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}' "$C"

# The assertion: /app/data must be a real mount, not a directory inside the container.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' "$C" | grep -c '"Destination":"/app/data"'   # must be 1

# Positive: the app has actually written its database into it.
sudo docker exec "$C" ls /app/data | grep -c 'mydb.sqlite'                             # must be 1
```

## Licence, since it is a fair question

ConvertX is AGPL-3.0. Running the official image unmodified, for yourself, in your own account, is
exactly the intended use. If you modify it and let other people use it over the network, section 13
says you owe those users the modified source. Unmodified, upstream's own repository covers that.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The flavor and the hourly rate in this file are reasoning from the Dockerfile
  and the source, not measurements: nobody has run this recipe on real infrastructure yet. When
  somebody does, replace this line with what actually happened and correct the estimates. The three
  numbers most worth capturing, because upstream publishes none of them, are the unpacked image
  size, the free disk after the pull, and the idle memory.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

services:
  convertx:
    image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      # Signing key for the session cookie. Generated for this deployment and
      # passed in via the project .env — never the README's published value, and
      # never left unset (it would be regenerated on every container restart).
      JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED:value]}
      # The first POST /register owns the instance regardless of this flag, so
      # it only protects the SECOND account onward. Claim the account, then this
      # keeps everyone else out.
      ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION: "false"
      # redu terminates TLS at its proxy; the public URL is https, so the
      # Secure session cookie must stay Secure.
      HTTP_ALLOWED: "false"
      # Public hostname: anonymous use would be an open disk-fill / CPU-burn
      # primitive, with no upload size limit anywhere in the app.
      ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED: "false"
      # The only garbage collector there is. 0 disables it and the disk grows
      # until it is full.
      AUTO_DELETE_EVERY_N_HOURS: "24"
      # 0 means unlimited, and one job of N files then starts N ffmpeg /
      # LibreOffice processes at once. On 2 vCPU / 4 GB that is an OOM kill.
      MAX_CONVERT_PROCESS: "3"
      # Cosmetic: date formatting and UI language only.
      TZ: Europe/London
      LANGUAGE: en-GB
      # WEBROOT is deliberately unset: it prefixes every route, including
      # /healthcheck, and there is nothing to prefix on a dedicated hostname.
    volumes:
      # Everything durable: data/mydb.sqlite, data/uploads/, data/output/.
      # A named volume, not a bind mount into the project dir, because a source
      # re-upload replaces that dir and the container runs as root.
      - convertx-data:/app/data

volumes:
  convertx-data:

input.redu_md:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/C4illin/ConvertX
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: none (the app is SQLite-only; the volume IS the database)
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: convertx
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST PERSON TO POST /register OWNS THE INSTANCE, AND ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false DOES NOT STOP THEM. This is the quirk that would break the deploy, and it is by design rather than a bug. src/pages/user.tsx:16 reads FIRST_RUN once at module load (true when the users table is empty), and :186 gates registration on `if (!ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION && !FIRST_RUN)`, so while FIRST_RUN holds the flag is bypassed and the account is created anyway. There is also no admin ROLE to grant: src/db/db.ts:9-13 shows the users table is (id, email, password) and nothing else, so the first account is simply the only account, and it is the administrator by virtue of being the one that exists. The window opens the moment redu's hostname resolves and NO SETTING CLOSES IT. The only thing that closes it is claiming the account. Do that as part of the deploy, before you hand over the URL, then run the check script in the body of this file to prove it took."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH BEFORE THE ACCOUNT IS CLAIMED: GET / returns 302 to /setup (src/pages/root.tsx:23-25) and /setup serves a Create your account form to anyone (user.tsx:68-128). GET /healthcheck is deliberately unauthenticated and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"} on any instance. Everything else, upload, convert, download, history and account, requires a valid auth cookie. AFTER the account is claimed, GET / and GET /register both 302 to /login and the setup page is unreachable. Note public/robots.txt ships Disallow: / for the whole app, which discourages crawlers and protects nothing: assume the URL is discoverable the moment it exists."
  - "⛔ NEVER SET ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME. Upstream's own comment on it says `only set this to true locally`, and the reason is worth spelling out. src/pages/root.tsx:33-57 hands every anonymous visitor a freshly signed 24-hour cookie and full use of the service, and src/index.tsx:30 sets maxRequestBodySize to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so there is no upload size limit of any kind. On a public URL that combination is an open disk-fill and CPU-burn primitive against the user's own VM, running ffmpeg, LibreOffice and ImageMagick on files a stranger chose. It defaults to false (src/helpers/env.ts:6-7); leave it there. UNAUTHENTICATED_USER_SHARING only matters when it is on, and would additionally pool every anonymous visitor's conversion history into one shared account."
  - "⛔ GENERATE YOUR OWN JWT_SECRET AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. THIS IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. Two ways to get it wrong and they fail differently. Leave it UNSET and src/pages/user.tsx:25 falls back to randomUUID() at every boot, so every session is invalidated on every container restart and the symptom reads as a broken login rather than a missing variable. COPY THE ONE IN THE README, or the one in upstream's compose.yaml, and you have shipped a signing key that is published in a repo with 18.5k stars: anyone who has read the README can mint a valid auth cookie for user id 1 and walk in. Generate one long random value of your own, pass it, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy."
  - "⛔ LEAVE HTTP_ALLOWED=false. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and the public URL is https, so the Secure session cookie set at user.tsx:229 and :354 (`secure: !HTTP_ALLOWED`) works correctly. The README suggests setting HTTP_ALLOWED=true as the fix for `can't login`, which is right for a plain-HTTP LAN box and wrong here: on a public internet hostname it downgrades the session cookie for no benefit. If login genuinely fails on redu, the cause is something else."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO DATABASE OPTION. DO NOT PROVISION A MANAGED POSTGRES FOR THIS. src/db/db.ts:2-5 opens bun:sqlite at the hardcoded path ./data/mydb.sqlite with no env var to redirect it, and no other driver exists anywhere in the source. A managed database would bill at GBP 0.0174/hr and hold nothing. The volume IS the database, which makes the next quirk the most important one in this file after the ownership race."
  - "⛔ ONE VOLUME ON /app/data, AND USE A NAMED VOLUME, NOT A BIND MOUNT. Everything durable lives under it: the sqlite file (src/db/db.ts:5), every upload (./data/uploads/, src/index.tsx:22) and every converted output (./data/output/, :23). Without it a redeploy loses the accounts, the history and every file, and the instance comes back on /setup with the ownership window reopened. Prefer a named volume over upstream's `./data` bind mount for two reasons: a path inside the project directory is exactly what a source re-upload replaces, and the container runs as root (the Dockerfile has no USER directive), which is what produces the `unable to open database file` error the README tells you to fix with chown. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a negative check alone is worthless: see the docker inspect block in the body of this file, whose first command exists purely to prove the container name resolved before the second command's answer is allowed to mean anything."
  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT HERE, NOT RAM, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS m1.medium RATHER THAN m1.small. Docker Hub's tag API reported full_size 1,554,975,448 bytes for v0.18.0 on 2026-08-17, about 1.55 GB COMPRESSED; upstream publishes no unpacked figure and this recipe has not been run, so the on-disk size is unknown but certainly larger, because Dockerfile:45-100 installs texlive with three extra collections, LibreOffice, Calibre, Inkscape, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, Ghostscript, ffmpeg and markitdown. On top of that every conversion keeps BOTH the uploaded input and the generated output on the same disk until the cleaner runs. m1.small ships 20 GB and that is not enough headroom to be comfortable; m1.medium ships 40 GB. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy, so put this in front of the user BEFORE sizing. Record the real numbers on the first run."
  - "AUTO_DELETE_EVERY_N_HOURS IS THE ONLY GARBAGE COLLECTOR, AND SETTING IT TO 0 TURNS IT OFF. It defaults to 24 (src/helpers/env.ts:9-11). src/index.tsx:72-97 runs a setTimeout chain from boot that deletes every job older than N hours, together with its upload and output directories, every N hours. Set it to 0 and nothing is ever deleted and the disk grows until it is full, which on a file converter is a matter of use rather than of time. Keep it at 24 or lower, and say plainly in the handover that converted files are TEMPORARY: this is a converter, not storage."
  - "SET MAX_CONVERT_PROCESS TO A SMALL NUMBER. It defaults to 0, which means unlimited (src/helpers/env.ts:19-22), and 0 is not merely a permissive cap: src/converters/main.ts:142-148 returns the whole file list as ONE chunk when the size is 0, and :163 then starts every file in that chunk concurrently. A single job containing two hundred files therefore launches two hundred ffmpeg or LibreOffice processes at once, which on a 2 vCPU / 4 GB VM is an out-of-memory kill rather than a slow conversion. 2 to 4 is a sane value; it costs throughput on big batches and buys the instance staying up."
  - "ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION: LEAVE IT AT ITS DEFAULT OF false (src/helpers/env.ts:1-2) unless the user actually wants more accounts. With it off and one account existing, GET /register 302s to /login and POST /register 302s to /login, so nobody else can sign up. It protects the SECOND account onward and does nothing whatsoever about the first: see the ownership quirk at the top. If the user does want extra accounts, turn it on deliberately, after claiming the first one, and understand that anyone who finds the URL can then register."
  - "PIN THE IMAGE, AND MIND THE LEADING v IN THE TAG. Use ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 (or c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0 on Docker Hub, which carries the same tags). The compose in upstream's README writes `image: ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx` with NO tag at all, which resolves to :latest and will silently cross a release on the next pull. On 2026-08-17 Docker Hub reported identical full_size and last_updated for v0.18.0 and latest, so they are the same build today and will not be after the next release. Note the tags are v0.18.0 and v0.17.0 with the v, unlike several other entries in this library. There is also a :main tag built from every push to the main branch; it is not a release and does not belong in a recipe."
  - "PORT 3000, AND THE HEALTH PROBE IS /healthcheck. Dockerfile:109 exposes 3000 and src/index.tsx:68 listens on process.env.PORT || 3000. # Self-host ConvertX on redu

A file converter you own: over a thousand format pairs, one container, a public HTTPS URL, and no
files leaving your own VM. About GBP 20 a month.

## What this deploys

- **ConvertX** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **One volume on `/app/data`**, which holds the SQLite database, every upload and every
  converted file. This app has no database server; the volume is the whole of its storage.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.028/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy ConvertX on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Nobody owns it until you do.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the account,
and `ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false` does not stop them: the source bypasses that flag while the
users table is empty. There is no admin role to grant and no setting that closes the window. The
only thing that closes it is claiming the account, which the recipe does before handing over the
URL. The script below proves it took.

**Disk, not memory.** The image carries texlive, LibreOffice, Calibre, Inkscape, ImageMagick and
ffmpeg, and every conversion then keeps both the input and the output until the cleaner runs. That
is why this is an m1.medium with 40 GB rather than the cheaper 20 GB flavor. Growing it later is a
volume resize, not a redeploy.

**Everything is on the volume.** There is no managed database in this plan because ConvertX cannot
use one: it is SQLite-only, at a hardcoded path. Miss the volume and a redeploy loses the account,
the history and every file, and puts the sign-up form back on a public URL.

## Prove the instance is claimed

Run this after the deploy. It refuses to answer at all until it can show it is talking to ConvertX
rather than to redu's proxy, which returns 502 for roughly the first two and a half minutes.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a ConvertX instance is CLAIMED, i.e. that the first-account window is shut.
# Usage:  HOST=convertx-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud bash check-claimed.sh
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname, with no scheme}"
B=$(mktemp)

# (1) Gate: prove we are talking to ConvertX at all. Every assertion below is meaningless
#     against an error page, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthcheck")
case "$code" in
  502) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly."; exit 2 ;;
  200) : ;;
  *)   echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck answered $code, not 200."; exit 2 ;;
esac
grep -q '"status":"ok"' "$B" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck body is not ConvertX's."; exit 2; }

# (2) Positive control for step 3. A claimed instance renders a login page that names itself.
#     If this fails, the redirect check below cannot be read as a pass.
lcode=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
grep -q 'ConvertX | Login' "$B" ||
  { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login answered $lcode and did not render ConvertX's login page."; exit 2; }
echo "OK: ConvertX is up and its login page renders."

# (3) The assertion. Anonymous GET / must land on /login. /setup is the UNCLAIMED state:
#     it serves a create-your-account form to whoever asks.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/")
case "$loc" in
  */setup) echo "FAIL: / redirects to /setup. THIS INSTANCE IS UNCLAIMED. Claim it now."; rm -f "$B"; exit 1 ;;
  */login) echo "PASS: / redirects to /login, so an account exists and the window is shut." ;;
  *)       echo "INCONCLUSIVE: / redirected to '$loc', which is neither. Check by hand."; rm -f "$B"; exit 2 ;;
esac

# (4) And that nobody else can sign up behind you.
rcode=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/register")
if [ "$rcode" = "302" ]; then
  echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] /register redirects, so ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION is off."
else
  echo "WARN: GET /register answered $rcode, so registration is OPEN to anyone. Intended?"
fi
rm -f "$B"
```

## Prove the volume took

Both halves, on the VM. The first command exists only to prove the container name resolved: without
it, a zero from the second command could just as easily mean you typed the wrong name.

```bash
C=convertx   # or whatever the compose project named it; list with: sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'

# Positive: this must print the container's name. If it errors, STOP, everything below is void.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}' "$C"

# The assertion: /app/data must be a real mount, not a directory inside the container.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' "$C" | grep -c '"Destination":"/app/data"'   # must be 1

# Positive: the app has actually written its database into it.
sudo docker exec "$C" ls /app/data | grep -c 'mydb.sqlite'                             # must be 1
```

## Licence, since it is a fair question

ConvertX is AGPL-3.0. Running the official image unmodified, for yourself, in your own account, is
exactly the intended use. If you modify it and let other people use it over the network, section 13
says you owe those users the modified source. Unmodified, upstream's own repository covers that.

**ConvertX v0.18.0 → one VM on redu**

| | |
|---|---|
| Image | `ghcr.io/c4illin/convertx:v0.18.0` (pinned, pulled — nothing built) |
| VM | **m1.medium** — 2 vCPU / 4 GB / **40 GB disk**, flavor_id `3` |

| Storage | **one named volume on `/app/data`** — SQLite DB + uploads + outputs |
| Database | **none** — the app is SQLite-only at a hardcoded path; a managed PG would bill £0.0174/hr and hold nothing |
| Cost | **£0.0278/hr ≈ £20.29/mo**, billed hourly, deletable any time |

`plan_deploy` quoted **m1.large at £35.48/mo** — it upsizes any compose stack on principle, because it can't tell a pulled image from a built one. It also flagged the disagreement with `redu.md` itself. I'm holding m1.medium: the constraint here is **disk, not RAM** (texlive + LibreOffice + Calibre + ffmpeg in the image, and every conversion keeps input *and* output until the 24h cleaner runs). 40 GB is why it isn't the 20 GB m1.small. Disk can be resized later without a redeploy.

Config decided by the recipe, not by me: `JWT_SECRET` freshly generated (not the README's published one), `ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=false`, `HTTP_ALLOWED=false`, `ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false`, `AUTO_DELETE_EVERY_N_HOURS=24`, `MAX_CONVERT_PROCESS=3`, `WEBROOT` unset.

**One thing you need to know before I create anything:** the first person to POST `/register` owns the instance, and `ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION=false` does *not* stop them — the source bypasses that flag while the users table is empty. There's no admin role and no setting that closes the window; only an existing account does. So I'll claim the account myself the moment it's up, before I hand you the URL, and then prove it took.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wait for ConvertX to answer, then claim the first account IMMEDIATELY.
# The window between "hostname answers" and "account exists" is the whole risk.
set -u
HOST=convertx-t8706vz9.redu.cloud
EMAIL='«REDACTED:env:c5eef326»'
PASS='[REDACTED:value]'
B=$(mktemp)

# 1) Wait for the app itself, not redu's proxy (which 502s while the container starts).
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
  code=$(curl -sS -m 10 -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthcheck" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)
  if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -q '"status":"ok"' "$B"; then
    echo "UP: /healthcheck 200 with ConvertX's body after ${i} tries"
    break
  fi
  if [ "$i" = "240" ]; then echo "GAVE UP: last /healthcheck code=$code"; exit 2; fi
  sleep 5
done

# 2) Claim it. This is the only thing that closes the ownership window.
rcode=$(curl -sS -m 30 -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "https://$HOST/register" \
  --data-urlencode "email=$EMAIL" --data-urlencode "password=[REDACTED:value]")
echo "REGISTER: http $rcode"
head -c 400 "$B"; echo

# 3) Prove the window is shut: anonymous GET / must now go to /login, not /setup.
loc=$(curl -sS -m 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/")
echo "ROOT-REDIRECT: $loc"
rm -f "$B"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a ConvertX instance is CLAIMED, i.e. that the first-account window is shut.
# Usage:  HOST=convertx-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud bash check-claimed.sh
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname, with no scheme}"
B=$(mktemp)

# (1) Gate: prove we are talking to ConvertX at all. Every assertion below is meaningless
#     against an error page, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthcheck")
case "$code" in
  502) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run shortly."; exit 2 ;;
  200) : ;;
  *)   echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck answered $code, not 200."; exit 2 ;;
esac
grep -q '"status":"ok"' "$B" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthcheck body is not ConvertX's."; exit 2; }

# (2) Positive control for step 3. A claimed instance renders a login page that names itself.
#     If this fails, the redirect check below cannot be read as a pass.
lcode=$(curl -sS -o "$B" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
grep -q 'ConvertX | Login' "$B" ||
  { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login answered $lcode and did not render ConvertX's login page."; exit 2; }
echo "OK: ConvertX is up and its login page renders."

# (3) The assertion. Anonymous GET / must land on /login. /setup is the UNCLAIMED state:
#     it serves a create-your-account form to whoever asks.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/")
case "$loc" in
  */setup) echo "FAIL: / redirects to /setup. THIS INSTANCE IS UNCLAIMED. Claim it now."; rm -f "$B"; exit 1 ;;
  */login) echo "PASS: / redirects to /login, so an account exists and the window is shut." ;;
  *)       echo "INCONCLUSIVE: / redirected to '$loc', which is neither. Check by hand."; rm -f "$B"; exit 2 ;;
esac

# (4) And that nobody else can sign up behind you.
rcode=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/register")
if [ "$rcode" = "302" ]; then
  echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] /register redirects, so ACCOUNT_REGISTRATION is off."
else
  echo "WARN: GET /register answered $rcode, so registration is OPEN to anyone. Intended?"
fi
rm -f "$B"
